sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: GPT Academic is a web app that puts large language models to work on academic tasks. Its one-click plugins translate and polish papers, read LaTeX and PDF papers and summarise them, translate arXiv articles, explain code and generate comments.
sixtySeconds.problem: Researchers spend hours translating papers, fixing grammar in LaTeX and summarising long PDFs. GPT Academic bundles those jobs as plugins in one interface, with your choice of OpenAI or Chinese models like Qwen and GLM.
whoFor: Readers translating English or Chinese papers
Users of Chinese LLMs such as Qwen and GLM
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a large set of ready-made academic plugins, from arXiv translation to LaTeX proofreading, with support for many model providers in one app. The main README is in Chinese, with English and other translations in the docs folder.
requirements: An LLM API key (OpenAI, Qwen, GLM and others)

overview: You set API keys and options in config.py, or better in a private config_private.py that overrides it, or through environment variables. Several API keys can coexist, for example OpenAI and Azure keys in one setting.

Plugins cover paper translation and polishing, full PDF translation, arXiv paper translation, LaTeX grammar checking, Google Scholar related-work drafting, project code analysis, batch comment generation and Mermaid diagram rendering. Formulas show in both TeX and rendered form.
Optional extras add local models like ChatGLM and MOSS, which need more dependencies and a strong GPU. Several Docker images cover different capability sets. The project is GPL-3.0 licensed.

steps.title: Set your API key
steps.body: Put API_KEY and other settings in config_private.py (it overrides config.py) or in environment variables.

steps.title: Install dependencies
steps.body: Use the exact versions in requirements.txt.

steps.title: Create and activate an environment
steps.code:
conda create -n gptac_venv python=3.11
conda activate gptac_venv

steps.title: Install dependencies and run
steps.code:
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python main.py

steps.title: Choose a scheme in docker-compose.yml
steps.body: Keep the scheme you want (for example scheme 1, online models only, recommended for most people) and delete the others.

troubleshooting.solution: Install the exact versions pinned in requirements.txt; Python 3.9 to 3.11 is recommended.
Settings in config_private.py override config.py; check you edited the right file.
Local models need extra requirements files and enough GPU memory; see the README's optional steps.
